description: High availability for the module's guest: which node it fails over to, and how often its disk is replicated there.
_note: cluster:ha is a drift reconciler, but NOT a per-field one, and the difference matters. Most of what it repairs has no module field behind it at all — the HA resource being absent or not 'started', the node-affinity rule missing, the replication job missing, the guest sitting on the wrong node — because those follow from DECLARING cluster:ha, not from any field's value. The drift record is keyed by field, so those units cannot be expressed in it. Its state also spans three Proxmox subsystems (/cluster/ha/resources, /cluster/ha/rules, /cluster/replication) that must be reconciled together: re-pointing HANode changes the affinity rule AND recreates the replication job, one decision across two planes. So the existing loop stays and both fields are apply:'reconcile'; what the manifest adds is the declared cost of changing them.

HANode.description: Secondary node for High Availability. Defaults to the first node in configuration.json that differs from 'node'. Must be different from 'node' and have the same storage defined. HA is only active when 'cluster:ha' is in dependsOn.
HANode.changeNote: The failover node. Changing it re-points the node-affinity rule and recreates the ZFS replication job against the new target — which means a full initial re-sync, so it is IO-heavy and can take a long time. It is still in-place: the running guest is not moved, not rebooted, and stays served throughout. The move that DOES relocate a guest is cluster:vm's `node`, which defers to this service for an HA module.

replicationSchedule.description: Cron-style schedule for HA replication interval
replicationSchedule.changeNote: How often the guest's disk is replicated to the failover node — the bound on how much is lost if the primary dies. A `pvesr update`: it changes when the next run happens, nothing else.

haCpu.description: The CPU model the HA guest runs. 'common': the richest x86-64 level its node and HANode both offer (config/cluster-cpu.json) — 'host' when both offer the same features — so every move between them is live-safe; a newer CPU's extra instructions (AVX-512 …) are not used. 'host': the full CPU of the node it starts on; then a move between nodes with different CPUs is a stop and start (HA failback off, node drains relocate it), never a live migration.

values.common: Live-safe moves; the instructions both nodes share
values.host: The node's full CPU; moves between unlike CPUs stop and start the guest

haCpu.changeNote: Sets the module's cputype (common: the shared level; host: host) and the HA resource's failback. The new CPU model takes effect when the guest restarts — held until a restart is authorized, like any held hardware change.
